key_insight: A compact clinical decision model can handle repeated record-reading tasks efficiently, while a generalist language model formulates questions and synthesizes evidence.
clinical_relevance: This approach could support patient-record review and trial eligibility screening, with answer probabilities helping route uncertain cases to human review.
method: Trained a 4-billion-parameter model on 12.4 million question–answer pairs from 3.6 million patients.
Answered multiple typed questions in one forward pass without task-specific retraining.
Paired the model with language-model agents for cited longitudinal summaries and trial screening.
evidence_signal: On 963,408 held-out patients, CS1-4B outperformed open decision models up to 27B on 13 of 14 independently scored tasks; across 21 external datasets, aggregate performance approached the strongest tested 27B model with 6.4× faster inference in a matched workload.
watch_item: Benchmark performance does not establish clinical safety; deployment needs prospective validation, calibrated uncertainty estimates and human oversight.
paper_title: A general-purpose System One decision model for clinical records
